eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent marine layer stratus clouds and steady onshore flow from the Pacific are suppressing daytime heating at Los Angeles International Airport, the official observation site, keeping the highest temperature likely in the 68–69°F range according to current trader consensus. This typical early-June pattern, often called June Gloom, brings low clouds and marine air that limit solar warming along the coast while inland areas warm more. Official National Weather Service forecasts and recent model runs show little change in this setup through the afternoon, with minimal warming expected before the daily maximum. The outcome will resolve to the recorded high at KLAX, where similar conditions have historically capped temperatures well below seasonal averages near 75–80°F.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=LTFM

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from major global weather models position Istanbul for a daily high near 30–31 °C on June 4, driven by a strengthening subtropical ridge and light southerly flow that limits marine cooling from the Sea of Marmara. This aligns with the market’s heaviest liquidity on the 31 °C-or-higher and 30 °C bins, reflecting trader consensus on the current guidance. Climatologically, early-June maxima average 25–27 °C, so the elevated outlook represents a modest positive anomaly that could shift with the next model cycle. Updated runs from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and NOAA’s Global Forecast System, expected within 24–48 hours, will provide the next key data point for resolution of the highest temperature recorded at Istanbul Airport.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model guidance for Mexico City on June 4 shows daily maximum temperatures clustered near the early-June climatological average of 24°C, reflected in the market’s leading 34.5% probability for that outcome. Official long-range outlooks from Mexican meteorological authorities indicate no strong high-pressure anomalies or unusual moisture surges through the period, leaving resolution dependent on the precise timing and coverage of showers. Updated short-range forecasts in the next 48 hours will narrow the range.
